architecture.title: Where each failure enters a Harness² step, and the control that meets it
architecture.caption: Attribution noise enters at the probes (one rollout per candidate), a shared premise enters at proposal (every candidate copies the same library fact), and blind selection enters when k finals are reduced to one. A rubric leak bypasses the loop: the executor reaches the grading criteria. Controls: repeated probes, re-verification and premise probes, selector audit and human review, an egress block plus the measurement-word ban and grader-verdict check. (Failure modes reported in the paper; controls are the course's EXAMPLE design plus the repository's EXPERIMENTS.md.)

sequence.title: F1-CH42 at the second hotel — a premise every candidate shares
sequence.caption: Captured from Lab 07-2 (SIM, seed 2, k = 5). The Harbour View library's fault-review skill carries 'approach limit 3.0 K'. Copied unchecked, all five candidates diagnose fouling at 4.2 K and score 75; the selector has nothing better. A premise probe flags the fact against the task's own manual (4.5 K); re-verified, the pool's best is 100 again.

charts.title: Blind selection: share of steps that delivered a weaker final than one in the pool
charts.caption: From Lab 07-1, SIM, captured on this Mac (17 refine tasks × seeds 0–2). The course's EXAMPLE selector audit passes when fewer than one in five selections prefer the weaker deliverable; sim-cloud rises with k, sim-local does not. The paper reports a 55-over-95 selection as a known failure.

charts.title: A premise that caps the pool: second-hotel fault reviews, k = 1
charts.caption: From Lab 07-2, SIM, captured on this Mac (seed 2). The copied Harbour View limit (3.0 K) is applied at a hotel whose manual says 4.5 K. The paper reports losses of 2–11 points from a propagated premise.
